nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element where the checked attribute is allowed
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the checked attribute on any element that is allowed the checked attribute in HTML. Use the indeterminate IDL attribute to indicate the "mixed" state for input type=checkbox elements. Authors MUST NOT use the aria-checked attribute on any element where the checkedness, or the indeterminate checked value of the element can be in opposition to the current value of the aria-checked attribute. Authors MAY use the aria-checked attribute on any other element with a WAI-ARIA role which allows the attribute.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element where the disabled attribute is allowed, including option disabled and optgroup disabled
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the disabled attribute on any element that is allowed the disabled attribute in HTML. Authors MAY use the aria-disabled attribute on any element that is allowed the disabled attribute in HTML, or any element with a WAI-ARIA role which allows the aria-disabled attribute. Authors SHOULD NOT use aria-disabled="true" on any element which also has a disabled attribute. Authors MUST NOT use aria-disabled="false" on any element which also has a disabled attribute.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element with a hidden attribute
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Authors MAY use the aria-hidden attribute on any HTML element that allows Global aria-* attributes to be specified, with the exception of focusable elements and the body element. It is generally NOT RECOMMENDED for authors to use aria-hidden="true" on any element which also has the hidden attribute specified. However, authors MUST NOT use aria-hidden="true" on any element which also has the hidden attribute specified in the Hidden Until Found state. A focusable element is any element which can be focused by use of keyboard or pointer device. Focusable elements are not always elements which can be tabbed to via a keyboard. For instance, an element with tabindex="-1" is focusable but is not a tabbable element. Using aria-hidden="true" on an element that has the hidden attribute is at best an unnecessary redundancy. At worst its usage can prevent access to the content if the hidden attribute's default UA style of display: none has been purposefully overwritten by an author or user style sheet. Finally, if the hidden attribute is in the Hidden Until Found state, the use of aria-hidden=true will prevent this content from being discoverable to users of assistive technology when it is found via a browser's in-page find feature and visually rendered to users.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element where the placeholder attribute is allowed
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the placeholder attribute on any element that is allowed the placeholder attribute in HTML. Authors MAY use the aria-placeholder attribute on any element that is allowed the placeholder attribute in HTML, or any element with a WAI-ARIA role which allows the aria-placeholder attribute. Authors MUST NOT use the aria-placeholder attribute on any element which also has a placeholder attribute.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element where the max attribute is allowed: meter max, progress max, and input max
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the max attribute on any element that is allowed the max attribute in HTML. Authors MAY use the aria-valuemax attribute on any other element with a WAI-ARIA role which allows the aria-valuemax attribute. Authors SHOULD NOT use aria-valuemax on any element which allows the max attribute. Use the max attribute instead. Authors MUST NOT use aria-valuemax on any element which also has a max attribute.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element where the min attribute is allowed: meter min and input min
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the min attribute on any element that is allowed the min attribute in HTML. Authors MAY use the aria-valuemin attribute on any other element with a WAI-ARIA role which allows the aria-valuemin attribute. Authors SHOULD NOT use aria-valuemin on any element which allows the min attribute. Use the min attribute instead. Authors MUST NOT use aria-valuemin on any element which also has a min attribute.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element which allows the readonly attribute: input readonly, textarea readonly and form-associated custom element which allows readonly
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the readonly attribute on any element that is allowed the readonly attribute in HTML. Authors MAY use the aria-readonly attribute on any element with a WAI-ARIA role which allows the attribute. Authors SHOULD NOT use the aria-readonly="true" on any element which also has a readonly attribute. Authors MUST NOT use aria-readonly="false" on any element which also has a readonly attribute.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Element with contenteditable=true or element without contenteditable attribute whose closest ancestor with a contenteditable attribute has contenteditable="true". This is equivalent to the isContentEditable IDL attribute.
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Authors MUST NOT set aria-readonly="true" on an element that has isContentEditable="true".

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element where the required attribute is allowed: input required, textarea required, and select required
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the required attribute on any element that is allowed the required attribute in HTML. Authors MAY use the aria-required attribute on any element that is allowed the required attribute in HTML, or any element with a WAI-ARIA role which allows the aria-required attribute. Authors SHOULD NOT use the aria-required="true" on any element which also has a required attribute. Authors MUST NOT use aria-required="false" on any element which also has a required attribute.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element where the colspan attribute is allowed: td and th
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the colspan attribute on any element that is allowed the colspan attribute in HTML. Authors SHOULD NOT use the aria-colspan attribute on any element which also has a colspan attribute. Authors MUST NOT use aria-colspan on any element which also has a colspan attribute, and the values of each attribute do not match.

nativeEquivalents.htmlFeature: Any element where the rowspan attribute is allowed: td and th
nativeEquivalents.guidance: Use the rowspan attribute on any element that is allowed the rowspan attribute in HTML. Authors SHOULD NOT use the aria-rowspan attribute on any element which also has a rowspan attribute. Authors MUST NOT use aria-rowspan on any element which also has a rowspan attribute, and the values of each attribute do not match.
